objectives.title: Explain net force and inertia
objectives.q: What are net force and inertia, and why do they together decide how an object's motion changes?
seeds: How exactly do we add two forces that point in different directions?
Can you show a worked example where the net force is not zero?
How is inertia related to mass, and is it the same as weight?

objectives.title: Distinguish speed, velocity and acceleration
objectives.q: What is the difference between speed, velocity and acceleration, and how does each describe a body's motion?
seeds: How do you add or subtract velocities that point in different directions?
Why does turning at constant speed still count as acceleration?
How will acceleration connect to force in Newton's second law?

objectives.title: Apply Newton's first law to bodies in equilibrium
objectives.q: How does Newton's first law describe a body at rest or moving at constant velocity when the net force is zero?
seeds: How do I apply the first law separately to horizontal and vertical forces?
What happens the instant the forces stop balancing?
How is the first law different from the second law?

objectives.title: Identify inertial reference frames
objectives.q: What is an inertial reference frame, and how can you tell whether Newton's first law holds in a given frame?
seeds: What exactly is a fictitious force, and why do we sometimes use one?
How large is the error in treating the Earth as inertial?
Does the second law also require an inertial frame?

objectives.title: Explain F = ma and the role of mass
objectives.q: What does Newton's second law F = ma mean, and what role does mass play in it?
seeds: How do I find the net force before using F = ma?
Why is weight equal to mass times gravitational field strength?
What happens to acceleration if the force keeps changing?

objectives.title: Calculate acceleration from net force
objectives.q: How do you calculate the acceleration of a simple one-body system from its net force and mass?
seeds: How do I combine forces that act at an angle to each other?
How do I get distance travelled from the acceleration?
What changes when the mass itself changes during the motion?

objectives.title: Apply Newton's third law to action-reaction pairs
objectives.q: How do you use Newton's third law to identify the equal and opposite force pairs in an interaction?
seeds: If the forces are equal, why does the bullet fly but the gun barely move?
How does the third law relate to conservation of momentum?
Why are weight and the normal force not an action-reaction pair?
